_comment: The single retrievable location every vault gate and index generator reads.
docs/knowledge-base -- 'The repository is one vault with one spine' requires the
declared set to be closed and to name each root governed or exempt, with a reason.
A gate must never decide its own subject: if a directory is neither governed nor
exempt here, the gate fails rather than skipping it.

note_roots._comment: GOVERNED. Tracked markdown here is a note. Which obligations apply is stated per-scope below.

_comment: EXEMPT. Tracked markdown here is not a note and carries no obligation of this
capability. Each entry states what owns the files instead. This list is the
declaration the spec requires; it is NOT a scanner convenience, and every gate
reports it as excluded coverage on every run.
exempt_roots..claude: Agent-harness files whose frontmatter keys and file layout are owned by the Claude Code loader and by vendored upstream skills. This repository does not author their format and cannot impose a classification on it.
exempt_roots.reference: Read-only prior art, untracked by design (.gitignore). Cited by file:line only; obtaining instructions and pinned revisions live in the spine.
exempt_roots.graphify-out: Generated code map. Layer 5 of the precedence order; regenerated from the AST, never hand-edited, and not part of the hand-written vault.
exempt_roots..github: Forge configuration: workflow files, the pull-request template and CODEOWNERS, whose location and format are owned by the hosting service. The template is nonetheless held byte-identical to the block stating it in docs/code/reviewing.md by ci/gates/review_obligations.py -- exempt from the vault's authoring obligations is not exempt from single-sourcing.

_comment: Paths excluded from a gate's traversal for a reason OTHER than root exemption.
Deliberately separate from exempt_roots: these are test inputs, not policy.
Anything here that is not also justified below fails the undeclared-exclusion check.
scan_excludes.ci/broken-inputs: Deliberately violating inputs. Each gate is proven to FAIL on these, so they must not be scanned as part of the real tree.
scan_excludes.ci/generator-inputs: Generator violating inputs and their pinned expected outputs. Deliberately partial trees and deliberately stale expectations, held so a generator is checked against something other than its own re-run; not part of the vault.

entry_points._comment: Reachability is measured from these. docs/knowledge-base -- 'Every note is reachable from an entry point'.

_comment: Paths this change declares out of its own scope, asserted byte-unchanged by
ci/gates/out_of_scope.py. docs/knowledge-base -- 'An artifact declared out of
scope stays byte-unchanged'. The reason these are listed rather than trusted:
/opsx:update reconciles neighbouring artifacts in ANY direction over
glob-expanded spec paths, and forbids only their creation, never their revision.
out_of_scope._baseline_comment: A FIXED commit, not a moving ref. This read 'HEAD', which the gate resolves per run, so the byte-unchanged assertion four tasks across two changes depend on caught an uncommitted edit and passed a committed one -- proven by appending a sentence to a frozen spec in a copied tree, which failed before the commit and passed after it. RE-BASELINED from fb24a9f to 26d2927: the sixteen specifications were legitimately revised by spec/expectations-terminator-dispatch, which adds fourteen requirements and fifty-three scenarios on expectations, a client-facing terminator accept path and cross-instance dispatch. That revision is not this declaration's subject; the two documentation changes are. So the baseline moves to the commit holding the revision, and the assertion continues to mean exactly what it meant: the documentation work has not touched these files. Moving it was a deliberate act, which is the whole point of pinning -- a moving ref would have let the revision through unnoticed and told nobody. RE-BASELINED AGAIN, from 26d2927 to d56484c, for a different reason: 26d2927 was reachable from nothing. The branch the entry above names, spec/expectations-terminator-dispatch, no longer exists, so that commit survived only as a dangling object in one local store -- no branch or tag contained it, `git fsck --unreachable` reported it, and `git gc --prune` would have deleted it. The consequence was that this gate passed only where it was written: `git clone --no-local` followed by `make check` failed with 'baseline ref 26d2927 does not resolve', so the one command this repository tells a reader to run could not pass for the reader, and no clone depth recovers a commit that is in no history. A pin only its author can resolve is not a pin. The move is not a weakening and does not re-open the frozen set: `git diff 26d2927 d56484c -- openspec/changes/rebuild-plugboard/specs` is empty, so the sixteen specifications are byte-identical at both commits and the assertion continues to mean exactly what it meant. d56484c is on main, so every clone resolves it.
out_of_scope._expiry_comment: A declaration cannot outlive its reason. This set exists because the two changes named in declared_by must not edit those specifications; it does NOT mean the specifications are frozen forever, and with a pinned baseline it would read that way. So the gate fails once every declaring change has been archived, demanding the declaration be removed rather than quietly asserting a freeze nobody decided on. A LEGITIMATE revision -- there is one in flight on the branch spec/expectations-terminator-dispatch, 14 requirements and 53 scenarios -- requires re-baselining or retiring this declaration, which is a deliberate visible act rather than a silent pass. That is the whole point of pinning: changing these files takes a decision, not an oversight.
out_of_scope._declared_by_comment: Re-declared from restructure-docs-as-vault and harden-vault-harness to rebuild-plugboard when those two archived on 2026-09-12. ci/gates/out_of_scope.py fails once every declaring change is archived -- the step docs/method/follow-ups.md names as what ends the freeze. Retiring the declaration outright is not the cheap option it looks like: the gate requires paths, declared_by and baseline_ref to be present, so removal means retiring the gate, its rule note, its violating input and its roster entries. The sixteen specifications are still not this change's subject, so the assertion continues to mean what it meant.

_comment: Closed value sets read by ci/gates/frontmatter.py. The note-class -> value
assignment table is populated by task 3.0, before any note is written or moved.
Scope: the spine and the per-component roots. The planning directories are
excluded -- an external tool authors and validates their format.
Which files under a planning directory are reachability subjects. A
planning artifact is a file an AUTHOR writes -- a proposal, a spec, a
design, a task list. Metadata the planning tool manages for itself is
not a subject: requiring a note to link to .openspec.yaml would be a
gate demanding prose about a tool's bookkeeping. Declared here rather
than inferred by the gate, because a gate that decides for itself which
files it will not look at is the defect the root set exists to remove.
Every note class this change creates, with the type and authority that
class carries. `status` is per-note, not per-class -- a note is current,
planned or superseded according to whether its subject exists -- so each
class declares the value a note of that class takes WHEN WRITTEN; the
currency gate is what moves it afterwards, and a stale marker fails.
A class present here with a missing field fails the frontmatter gate:
which authority a glossary carries versus a decision note was a design
decision the plan had left to nobody.

moc.description: A map of content: start-here and any hand-written wayfinding note. Carries no claim of its own.

essay.description: Long-form argument -- the orientation prose the numbered essays become. Records why, never what.

concept.description: One domain concept explained for orientation. Links to the specification that owns its behaviour.

capability.description: The concept note for one capability. Links to its specification, its dependencies and the decisions that shaped it; restates no requirement.

decision.description: One decision in force, linking into its entry in the declared register rather than restating it.

glossary.description: Domain vocabulary. Rationale rather than normative: the specifications fix the terms, this collects them.

rule.description: One named obligation on how code is written or placed, naming its gate or carrying the no-gate marker.

banned-pattern.description: One prohibited construct with its own anchor, naming the defect it prevents and citing it.

procedure.description: An ordered task-shaped procedure -- adding a feature, fixing a bug -- naming its own verification.

guide.description: Practitioner guidance that is neither one rule nor one concept: language conventions, component boundaries.

index.description: Generated by a tool, byte-identical to a fresh regeneration, never hand-edited.

entry.description: A router an agent or a person reads first. Held to a size ceiling and to the absent-artifact rule rather than to classification.

_comment: docs/knowledge-base -- 'There is exactly one decision register'. A register
assigns identifiers in the installation's unnamespaced D<n> sequence and
holds those decisions as being in force. There is one, named here, so the
gate has a declared subject instead of a path convention.
A change's own design rationale may record decisions under a namespace;
a namespaced set is NOT a register. This change's own ten decisions were
D1-D10, colliding one-for-one with the register's -- the defect the change
calls BREAKING, committed in the act of fixing it. They are now RDV1-RDV10.
Permanently unassigned. The surviving register jumped D10 -> D16, and the
superseded register filled D11-D15 with five decisions of its own. Reusing
a number would make a citation written today ambiguous against any
citation written against the old register, including archived ones -- so
the numbers are retired rather than recycled, and each records what it
used to denote and where that decision lives now.
retired.D11: was 'Proxied traffic terminates before application middleware' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D5
retired.D12: was 'Framing authority is per-hop, never relayed' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D6
retired.D13: was 'Tenant scoping in the data model' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D8
retired.D14: was 'Domain ownership verification precedes certificate issuance' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D9
retired.D15: was 'Observability before the hot path' in docs/05-decision-log.md; now D27

per_change_namespaces._comment: A change's own decisions carry a prefix naming the change.

_comment: Paths whose notes are ABOUT the register rather than being one. A heading
here may name an identifier ONLY if the register already holds it, and
only in a file that links to the register -- so the note is a pointer,
not a restatement.
This exists because a decision note's natural title is '# D1 - Title',
which a heading-means-assignment heuristic reads as opening a second
register. Both looser fixes were rejected: allowing any already-assigned
identifier in any heading would let a second register REDEFINE D1 while
D1 exists, which is the exact collision the requirement prevents; and
retitling the notes to dodge the regex would bend the vault to the gate.
An unassigned identifier, a retired one, or a file with no link to the
register still fails here.
Every identifier a superseded register used, what it denoted there, and
what it denotes now -- so a citation written against the old register
resolves rather than being guessed at. `now` is either an identifier in
the surviving register or the literal 'retired'.
A register may not be removed while it holds a decision recorded nowhere
else, and this table is what makes that check an enumeration rather than
an inspection.

D1.denoted: Rebuild from scratch, reference as prior art only

D4.denoted: Version skew is the governing constraint

D8.denoted: Capability negotiation with refusal, not degradation

D11.denoted: Proxied traffic terminates before application middleware

D12.denoted: Framing authority is per-hop, never relayed

D13.denoted: Tenant scoping in the data model

D14.denoted: Domain ownership verification precedes certificate issuance

decision_register._prefix_comment: The letter the installation's unnamespaced sequence uses. Declared rather than hardcoded in ci/gates/decision_register.py, because a gate never decides its own scope and the rule the vault states is that an identifier belongs to a declared register -- not that the letter D is special. Generalising the requirement to an arbitrary identifier family was drafted, prototyped, and cut: 483 findings and zero true positives, because a tokenizer loose enough to see a new family also sees SHA, IPv and PBKDF. This is the part of it worth having.

_comment: Artifacts cited by file:line that are NOT tracked in this repository. Each
must name the note stating how to obtain it and the revision the citations
were taken against, so a citation into it is checkable by someone other
than its author. docs/knowledge-base -- 'A cited artifact is obtainable'.
Of 294 citations on the current tree, 9 are written prefixed into reference/
and 227 are unqualified and attributed to it: 236 in all, checkable by
nobody but their author until the revisions above are reachable. Reproduce
with `python3 ci/gates/citations.py`, which prints the breakdown on every
run. This read '139 citations' when the declaration was written -- the
figure for the pre-restructure tree at fb24a9f, never recomputed, and a
number in prose that no command reproduced.
cited_artifacts._unqualified: A citation with no directory component -- `mount_store.ex:402` -- is resolved first by basename against the tracked set, and otherwise attributed to 'prior_art_default' below. Stated because it is a real weakening: an unqualified citation is less checkable than a prefixed one. 227 of the 294 citations on the current tree are written that way, printed on every run by ci/gates/citations.py; this read 'roughly seventy' and was never recomputed.

_comment: Words that make a sentence an obligation. A spine note may not state
behaviour a specification owns, so these are refused in the spine outside a
quote, a code span or a fenced block. This is the DECIDABLE half of the
citation requirement -- see ci/gates/citations.py for what it does not decide.
Read by ci/gates/binary_assets.py. Every tracked binary appears here with its
origin and the terms it is carried under; anything else fails. Empty today,
and that is the intended steady state -- the prior attempt shipped 85 JPEGs
whose origin was established nowhere, and two compiled Go commands reached a
commit in THIS repository before the check existed, left by `go build ./...`
writing into a module root. Adding a binary is now a deliberate edit here,
which is a place a reviewer looks.
Which gates block, and which task flips each remaining one. A gate that
cannot pass on the tree it governs is not a gate, so a gate lands in
report-only and becomes blocking at the task that makes the tree satisfy
it. This is the record tasks.md 1.11 requires; the gate ROSTER is not
here -- it is discovered from ci/gates/*.py against ci/broken-inputs/*,
because a declared roster is a second encoding of what the tree states.
Gates whose subject is a WHOLE-TREE property rather than a per-file one.
A minimal violating input necessarily fails every one of these -- it has no
entry point, no generated index, no reader config, no conventions note -- so
they are excluded from the fixture-isolation check in ci/gates/meta.py.
Running that check over all twenty gates produced 165 failures, none of them
a defect: satisfying it literally would mean building twenty complete valid
vaults, one per fixture. The isolation property that MATTERS is still
checked: a fixture must not trip another PER-FILE gate, and every fixture
must fail its own gate by its own logic (the neuter test).

The runner, correspondences and generators gates are added by harden-vault-harness: no fixture tree holds a workflow file, a rule index, a gate roster or a ci/gen tool, so each would otherwise fail on all 27 trees through the isolation check. The count is three, not the two that change's task 1.4 estimated; measured at task 4.

coverage is added for the same reason: its subject is the gate roster, so it invokes every gate-shaped module it finds. Two fixtures carry stray .py files under ci/gates for their own cases -- rule-gate-correspondence needs a gate naming no rule note, language-coverage needs Python present -- and neither is a gate roster. Running the isolation check over them reported two failures, neither a defect.
fixture-declarations is added for the same reason: its subject is the whole violating-input set, so a minimal tree carrying one fixture of its own is not that set.

top-level-readmes is added by rebuild-plugboard task 1.1 for the same reason: its subject is every top-level directory of a tree, and a minimal violating input has one or two of them with no README by construction. Running the isolation check over the other fixtures would have reported a failure on nearly every one, none of them a defect.

review-obligations is added for the same reason: its subject is the canonical review note and the artifacts declared to enumerate it, and no fixture tree holds either, so it reports the canonical note absent on every other tree. Its own fixture carries both, so the neuter test and the per-file isolation check still bind.

test-tiers is added by rebuild-plugboard task 2.7: its subjects are the shared make includes and the top-level Makefile at fixed paths, none of which any other fixture tree carries, so it would fail on every one of them for absence rather than for a defect.

expected-outcomes is added by rebuild-plugboard task 4.5: its subject is ci/expected-outcomes.json at a fixed path, which no other fixture tree carries, so it would fail on every one of them for absence rather than for a defect.
A gate whose subject set is legitimately empty on the tracked tree, with
the reason and the work that ends it. An UNdeclared empty subject set
fails; a declared one passes and states both on every run; and once the
named work is complete while the set is still empty, the build fails, so a
declaration cannot outlive its reason. Previously this reason lived in
ci/gates/component_boundaries.py's docstring, where nothing could read it.

Empty of entries as of rebuild-plugboard task 1.1: component-boundaries was the only declarant, and its five directories now exist. The mechanism stays declared because the next gate to land ahead of its subject needs it.
A directory under ci/broken-inputs whose violating inputs are verified by a
SCRIPT rather than by ci/gates/<name>.py. The naming rule pairs an input to a
gate module; these pair to a checker that starts external processes against a
copy of a component, which is work `make check` must not do -- it is the one
command a contributor runs on every commit. Declared so a directory with no
gate module of its name reads as a decision rather than as an orphan.

ci/broken-inputs/proxy-tooling.subject: the lint recipe of ci/make/elixir.mk, reached as `make -C proxy lint`
ci/broken-inputs/proxy-tooling.why_not_a_gate: Six external processes against a copied tree, six times over -- about fifty seconds warm. A gate's subject is a property of the tree and it starts no process.

ci/broken-inputs/recording-origin.subject: the assertion suite conformance/recorder exports, proven to REJECT a deliberately map-backed recorder
ci/broken-inputs/recording-origin.why_not_a_gate: Its own Go module with a replace directive, compiled and run. ci/broken-inputs is a declared scan exclusion, so nothing there is reachable from a component's build and the proof has to be pulled in from the other side.

_comment: Vault reader settings that change how links resolve and how notes are classified
are tracked; per-person workspace state and caches are not. docs/knowledge-base --
'The repository is one vault with one spine'.
Where a capability's concept note lives, and how its filename derives from
its identifier. docs/knowledge-base -- 'Each capability has a concept note'.
The correspondence is gated in the direction that can drift: a dependency
named inside a specification with no matching link in the concept note fails.
RDV5 deliberately builds the graph in the vault rather than by editing the
82 backticked cross-references inside the specifications themselves.
capability_notes._ceiling_comment: Declared empirically from the first four notes written, per task 5.1: they came in at 61/66/67/73 lines and the widest capability in the remaining twelve (operability/packaging, nine dependency edges) reached 78. 80 fits every note with headroom and without inviting essays. A note over it is a finding.

_comment: docs/code-standards. Rule notes live under these directories; the quarantine
holds the unenforced ones so a preference is distinguishable from an
obligation without reading either note. The organising line is inherited:
'a rule with no gate is a wish' -- so the guide is arranged by enforcement
rather than by topic, and the correspondence is checked BOTH ways.
Components whose boundary must be stated, keyed on the set that EXISTS. All
five directories were created by rebuild-plugboard task 1.1, so the set is no
longer empty and the gate no longer passes vacuously -- its declared_vacuity
entry was removed by that same task, which is the mechanism working rather
than a tidy-up. Adding a component now means adding its boundary note in the
same change, and deleting one means deleting the note.
The platform set ci/gen has no part in: conformance/Makefile's build target
reads it, so the declaration and the artifacts cannot disagree. The suite is
handed to someone writing a sidecar in a language this repository has never
seen; a binary that needs a matching libc is where that offer fails first,
which is why the build is CGO-free rather than merely cross-compiled.
Read by ci/gates/linter_config.py. One configuration for every Go module,
one copy of it, and one copy of the recipes that invoke it. recognised_names
is golangci-lint's own set rather than the one file this repository uses: a
second copy added as .golangci.yaml would otherwise be invisible to the check
that exists to find a second copy.
The three tiers, read by ci/fast-tier.py and ci/gates/test_tiers.py. The
budget lives here rather than in the tool or in the rule note, so the number
the rule states and the number enforced cannot become two numbers -- which is
the failure the correspondences gate exists for, in miniature.
Every component exposes all three targets; a tier with no tests in a given
component is a no-op there, never a missing target, because a dispatch that
silently skips a component is the shape this repository keeps refusing.
Read by ci/gates/banned_patterns.py. Five project-specific prohibitions no
off-the-shelf linter expresses. header_tokens is what makes check 1 decidable:
the construct alone is legitimate, and the check fires only where the line also
names a header field. That trades false negatives for zero false positives on
purpose -- a check firing on every map[string]string is turned off within a
week, and a rule with no enforcement is worse than one with partial.
notes maps each check to the note stating it, so a failure hands over the rule
rather than a verdict.
Read by ci/gates/size_ceilings.py, ci/gates/code_duplication.py and
ci/gates/no_repair.py through the shared reader ci/gates/_source.py. The
numbers live here and not in the gates, so the figure a rule note states and
the figure enforced cannot become two figures.

excluded_languages._comment: A language deliberately out of scope, with the reason and the work that ends it. Printed on every run: an exclusion nobody can see is an exemption.

.py.reason: The harness itself. Task 3.5 asks for the ceilings in 'both languages', meaning the two the components are written in, and four gate modules are over 300 non-comment lines today (ci/gates/out_of_scope.py at 442, links.py 340, wikilinks.py 305, citations.py 301). Holding the harness to its own ceiling is right and is a separate piece of work from building the gate.
.py.ends_with: a change that splits those four modules, recorded in docs/method/follow-ups.md

_comment: Read by ci/gates/no_repair.py. Two vocabularies, declared rather than written
into the gate: the words that make a path a WAIT, and the verbs that make a
call a REPAIR. Widening either to every verb would fire on every test, so the
residue is review's and the gate says so.
Read by ci/gates/test_hygiene.py. Abandoned reasoning committed as a comment,
which the audit found is the signature of a test written around a defect
rather than at it. Phrases rather than a heuristic: a check for 'uncertainty'
over English fires on every honest comment.
Read by ci/gates/top_level_readmes.py. Every top-level directory holding a
tracked file carries a README routing a reader to what owns it, unless it is
named here with the reason. Roots already declared in exempt_roots are exempt
from this obligation too and are NOT restated here -- two lists of the same
directories is the second encoding ci/gates/correspondences.py exists to catch.
An entry whose directory holds no tracked file fails: a declaration cannot
outlive its subject.

exempt.docs: The spine is entered through its generated index at docs/index.md, which ci/gen/indexes.py produces and ci/gates/index_drift.py holds byte-identical to a fresh regeneration. A hand-written README beside it would be a second entry for one directory, which is exactly what the reachability rule exists to prevent.
exempt.openspec: Layout owned by the OpenSpec CLI: it reads openspec/config.yaml and writes the change directories beneath. This repository does not author that format, and a README here would describe a tool's tree back at it.
exempt.ci: The harness is described once, in docs/method/harness.md, and every gate's rule note is reachable from docs/rule-index.md. A second description sitting beside the gate modules is the copy that drifts -- the same reason a component README links its boundary note instead of restating it.
exempt..obsidian: Reader configuration owned by Obsidian and checked by ci/gates/reader_config.py. What it holds is a vault's settings, not a component's boundary.

_comment: Keyed on the languages that hold tracked source. Today that is Python only

-- every gate module, the shared library and the generators, all tracked .py outside the fixtures (`git ls-files 'ci/*.py' | grep -vc broken-inputs`). This read 'the sixteen gate modules and the index generator', then '21 gate modules ... 26 tracked .py' after a recount that went stale within hours because gates were added the same day. The command is the figure; the prose no longer states one. Elixir and Go arrive
with their source; writing their conventions now would fail this gate's own
'conventions for an absent language are refused' case, and the proposal's
promise of them is therefore scoped to when their source lands.
Fixture files under ci/broken-inputs are test inputs, not source.
_source_extensions_comment: The second route to 'a language is present', and the one that makes
this gate's FIRST case reachable at all. Iterating source_globs alone
cannot find a language nobody has declared yet: `present` would be a
subset of what is already registered, so 'introducing a language
without its conventions fails' could only ever fire for a language
somebody had already registered a glob for -- and whoever remembers
the glob remembers the note. Elixir and Go source lands with
rebuild-plugboard tasks 2.1 and 2.3 -- task 1.1 creates the directories
and no source -- which is exactly when the rule has to bite, so the
enumeration names them now. Admitting a further language is a
deliberate edit here rather than a silent pass.

code_standards._gate_states: A rule note's Gate line is one of three: a runnable `ci/gates/<name>.py`; `none` (preference, quarantined, never a blocking objection); or `planned` (an obligation whose gate is not built yet, which must also be marked status: planned and link the work that builds it). The third state exists because the banned patterns are obligations today and their gates arrive with rebuild-plugboard task 3.7 -- filing them as `none` would record an obligation as taste, and claiming a gate would name one that does not run.

_comment: Generated files outside the per-directory index scheme, each with the tool
that produces it. ci/gates/index_drift.py runs each tool in check mode, so a
second generator cannot quietly become the one nothing verifies.
docs/rule-index.md carries every rule's enforcement status and the
proportion carrying no gate -- both properties of a table, so the table is
generated rather than maintained: a hand-written index of enforcement status
is a second encoding of what the notes say, and the two drift in the
direction that flatters the guide.
The authority precedence, stated in exactly one location. The gate looks for
an exact marker line rather than for ordered layer names: 'contract',
'specifications' and 'decisions' are ordinary words in this vocabulary, so a
name-based check reported almost every capability note as a restatement.
A note DEFERRING to its owner ('the specification wins where we disagree') is
required of every spine note and is not a restatement.
precedence.marker: AUTHORITY PRECEDENCE -- stated here and nowhere else

_comment: The routers an agent or a person reads first. The ceiling is the one the
plan already set for them (rebuild-plugboard task 1.3): 4 KB. CLAUDE.md was
4,865 bytes against it, roughly a kilobyte of which described a graphify
knowledge graph that has never been generated in this repository -- so the
absent-artifact check and the ceiling close on the same content.
THE single enumeration both authoring channels and the gates key on.
RDV10: no one channel reaches both authors. openspec/config.yaml's `rules:`
block is keyed per openspec artifact, so it cannot express an obligation on
a note; and a note author never reads it. So there are two channels, and a
convention added to the gates without reaching BOTH fails.
Each id maps to the gate that enforces it, so the keying is checkable rather
than a promise.

relative-links.statement: Relations are relative markdown links. No wikilinks, no transclusion, no absolute paths.

classification.statement: Every spine or component note declares type, status and authority from the closed enumerations.

reachable.statement: Every note is reachable by links from a declared entry point.

no-owned-behaviour.statement: A note never states behaviour a specification owns; no normative modal in the spine. Link the owner.

cited-or-unverified.statement: Every claim carries a citation into a tracked file or an obtainable artifact, or an explicit Unverified marker.

one-register.statement: One decision register. A change's own decisions carry a namespace; a retired identifier is never reused.

currency.statement: A planned note links the work that builds it, and its marker is retired once its subject exists.

precedence-once.statement: The authority precedence is stated in exactly one location; every other note links it.

one-copy.statement: Requirement text has one copy. Link the specification rather than restating it.

generated-indexes.statement: An index is generated, tracked, and byte-identical to a fresh regeneration. Never hand-edit one.

rule-names-gate.statement: Every rule note names its gate, or `planned`, or `none` (preference, quarantined).

capability-note.statement: Every capability has one concept note under the declared ceiling, linking its spec and its dependencies.

entry-routes.statement: An entry file routes, stays under its ceiling, and names nothing the repository does not contain.

declared-roots.statement: Every tracked note lives under a declared governed root; an exempt root records what owns its files.

_comment: The runner configuration the gates require. Declared rather than hardcoded
because a gate never decides its own scope (ci/gates/_common.py). The
PROVIDER is not a spec-level commitment: harden-vault-harness HVH2 keys the
requirement on these paths, so switching forge edits these values and the
files they name, and changes no requirement.
WORKFLOWS is a mapping rather than one path because CI runs more than one
job: D28's sign-off check is blocking on a pull request and reachable from
no local target, and until it was declared here nothing checked it -- every
property its header comment claimed for itself was prose. A second blocking
workflow outside the gate's declared scope is the exact condition the rule
behind this gate exists to refuse.
Each entry declares its OWN required triggers, so a workflow that
deliberately runs on fewer events states that as a decision a gate holds,
rather than differing from its sibling for no recorded reason.

.github/workflows/check.yml.why_these_triggers: Every gate's subject is the tree, so every event that changes the tree must run them.

.github/workflows/dco.yml.why_these_triggers: The subject is the set of commits a pull request proposes, which a push event does not define. Declared so the narrower trigger is a decision rather than an omission.

forbidden_clauses._comment: Each maps a configuration key to the refusal it would defeat.
forbidden_clauses.paths: a path filter lets a change touching only unlisted paths skip every gate
forbidden_clauses.branches: a branch filter lets work on an unlisted branch skip every gate
forbidden_clauses.continue-on-error: a non-zero exit that does not fail the job is a gate that cannot refuse

_comment: Every tool that produces a tracked artifact, with the violating input and
the pinned expected output that hold it to an oracle it cannot move.
Keyed on the TOOL, because ci/gen/indexes.py produces thirteen artifacts
under the per-directory index scheme and cannot be keyed on one of them --
it is the generator that generated_files below does not name, and that is
the defect this declaration closes. Fixtures live OUTSIDE ci/broken-inputs
(harden-vault-harness HVH5): ci/gates/meta.py maps a gate module to a
fixture directory there, and a generator fixture has no gate module.
Sets that two encodings resolve independently. Declared rather than
discovered: the trigger first drafted -- 'published in a tracked artifact a
reader is routed to' -- narrowed nothing, because an in-force requirement
already makes very nearly every tracked subject reachable from an entry point.
A side names a RESOLVER KIND the gate knows how to run and compares
MEMBERS, never a cardinal: an artifact stating a count without naming its
members is not a side, because a count cannot say which member diverged.

blocking-classification.subject: which gates the build treats as blocking

computed.members: gate ids derived from the modules under ci/gates that the runner invokes

published.members: gate ids this manifest classifies as blocking

_comment: A correspondence closed by collapsing both sides onto ONE resolver is
retired here with that resolver recorded, rather than deleted -- so that
re-opening the divergence requires undoing a named decision instead of
quietly adding a second encoding back.

rule-set.subject: every rule note, against the rows the rule index publishes
rule-set.divergence: docs/rule-index.md published 42 rules / 20 gated while ci/gates/rule_gate_correspondence.py counted 43 / 21 over the same set; the missing member was docs/method/authority-precedence.md, a gated rule absent from the index CLAUDE.md routes readers to
rule-set.reason: Both sides now call the one resolver in ci/gates/_common.py -- the gate and ci/gen/rule_index.py import it rather than each walking the tree -- so the two cannot diverge by construction and there is no longer a pair to reconcile.

_comment: The canonical enumerations and the artifacts obliged to enumerate them.
Declared rather than hardcoded because a gate never decides its own scope
(ci/gates/_common.py). The CITATION FORM is the key: an artifact names an
item by number, never by copying its text, because the rule is about
location rather than wording -- a second copy of the wording is what the
duplication gate already refuses. So adding item 10 to an enumeration here
fails every artifact under the obligation until it cites item 10.
Items are read from the canonical note, never declared as a count: a
cardinal in this file would be a second encoding of what that note states.
The pull-request template is STATED in the canonical note, inside the fenced
block under `heading`, and PUBLISHED at `path` where the forge reads it.
reviewing.md's own words: a template is the artifact most likely to be copied
and then left behind. So the published copy is held byte-identical to the
block stating it, in both directions, and editing either alone fails.
Read from the UNMASKED note: mask_fences blanks exactly the block this case
is about.
